title: UK grocery-supplier compliance can remain high while retailer processes transfer forecasting, payment and exit risk downstream
source_unit: UK Groceries Code Adjudicator, 2026 annual supplier survey results
geography: United Kingdom; suppliers to the 14 designated grocery retailers

observations.period: 2026 annual survey; supplier experience during the prior 12 months

denominator.unit: more than 2,600 supplier responses cited by the Groceries Code Adjudicator

code_issue.unit: percent of suppliers reporting a Groceries Code issue, up from 30% in 2025

no_issue.unit: share of suppliers reporting no issue with the designated retailers

overall_compliance.unit: average perceived compliance across the 14 designated retailers

observations.method: Confidential annual supplier survey conducted for the Groceries Code Adjudicator by YouGov; the official release reports aggregate supplier responses and retailer-level perceived compliance.
observations.uncertainty: The public release does not provide the response rate, weighting, supplier-size composition, item bases, confidence intervals, observed contract records, retailer response or supplier financial outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Direct suppliers to the 14 designated UK grocery retailers; results are not a survey of consumers or all food businesses.
observations.counterinterpretation: High perceived compliance and more than half reporting no issue indicate that the supplier relationship is not uniformly coercive; the aggregate issue increase may reflect reporting or composition change rather than generalized deterioration.

denominator.unit: supplier survey issue-category frame reported by the Groceries Code Adjudicator

invoice_discrepancy_resolution.unit: percent of suppliers raising issues with retailer processes for promptly resolving invoice discrepancies

inaccurate_forecasting_cost.unit: percent of suppliers reporting significant costs from inaccurate retailer forecasting

delisting_without_notice.unit: percent of suppliers reporting de-listing without reasonable notice

payment_delay.unit: percent of suppliers reporting delays in payment

observations.method: Official GCA summary of the 2026 confidential supplier survey; issue categories are reported as shares of respondents.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not establish the monetary size of costs, duration of delays, incidence by supplier size or category, contract remedies, or downstream consumer prices and availability.
observations.subgroup: Suppliers reporting one or more issues in their relationships with designated retailers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Issue reporting may identify effective regulatory visibility rather than total harm, and a reported issue does not establish unlawful conduct or an inadequate remedy in an individual case.

confidential_reporting_route.value: the GCA presents confidential and anonymous channels as part of its regulatory arsenal

deep_dive_interviews.value: YouGov follow-up interviews were commissioned to explore supplier experiences in greater detail

supplier_power_boundary.value: visibility of an issue and a regulator route do not establish payment, correction, switching or restored bargaining power

observations.method: GCA public release describing the survey, confidential reporting route and planned supplier deep-dive interviews.
observations.uncertainty: The public release does not report whether suppliers used the confidential route, whether retailers corrected issues, or whether supplier investment, employment, innovation, prices or product availability changed.
observations.subgroup: Direct grocery suppliers and the GCA-regulated retailer-supplier relationship.
observations.counterinterpretation: A regulator can improve contestability even before a measurable financial remedy appears; the absence of public remedy data is not proof that no remedy occurred.

related_sources.claim: The GCA announced a 29 September 2026 conference where YouGov would present a detailed analysis of the survey.
Official GCA 2026 annual survey information pack linked from the release.

boundary: This record adds a firm-sector power and contestability route: retailer compliance can remain high while forecasting, payment, invoice, de-listing and reporting conditions distribute risk across suppliers. It does not measure consumer prices, supplier profitability, unlawful conduct, completed remedy, switching, investment, employment, innovation or causal retailer effects.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official GCA 2026 annual supplier survey release was reviewed for response scale, compliance, issue prevalence, issue categories, confidential reporting and follow-up interview design.
